slides.title: NeuraFrame Studio Launches Embodied AI Memory Layer
slides.tldr: EMBODIED AI MEMORY LAYER FOR ROBOTS
slides.highlight: NeuraFrame Studio has introduced a memory layer that enables robots to learn without requiring onboard AI models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: UBTech Launches Hyper-Real Humanoid Robots for Lonely People
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced hyper-real humanoid robots designed to assist lonely individuals, providing a relevant case for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins
slides.tldr: EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL SIMULATIONS TO DIGITAL TWINS
slides.highlight: This work explores the transition from agent-based models to LLM-enhanced simulations and Social Digital Twins, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: A survey on the evolution of social simulations from rule-based agent-based modeling to LLM-enhanced digital twins.
card.key_idea: Transitions from classical ABMs (explicit rules) to LLM-ABMs (natural language reasoning) and Social Digital Twins (data-driven, high-fidelity replicas of specific real-world socio-technical systems).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via literature survey and references to studies on opinion dynamics, polarization, and echo chambers using LLM agents and network structures.
card.limitation: High sensitivity to prompt design, potential for model biases, resource-intensive maintenance, and risks of overfitting to specific system peculiarities.

slides.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
slides.highlight: This study examines how mutual and referential robot gazes affect human visual attention during a collaborative game, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Robot gaze orientation does not significantly affect human visual attention during a cognitively demanding collaborative game.
card.key_idea: Comparing mutual and referential robot gaze behaviors in an LLM-driven word association game using eye-tracking to measure human fixation and confirmation-seeking gaze patterns.
card.evaluation: 10 non-native English speakers; measured time to first fixation and gaze distribution. Results showed no statistically significant effect of robot gaze on fixation time.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=10) and potential cognitive load from non-native language use may have influenced the results.

slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive tactile sensing requirements from interaction data, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A requirement-driven framework using VR to determine optimal tactile sensor placement and resolution for social robots.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data is collected and offline-reconstructed to simulate various tactile sensor configurations, decoupling sensing requirements from hardware constraints before physical fabrication.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via two user studies (12 and 18 participants) and a 5,520-trial dataset using Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
card.limitation: Simulation uses only binary contact signals (no force/pressure) and resolution analysis was limited to the robot's arm.

slides.title: Breaking the 15% Barrier: A Real-World Data-Driven System for Proactive Social Robot Triggered by User Nonverbal Cues
slides.highlight: This research develops a system that enables social robots to proactively respond to nonverbal cues like waving or pointing, enhancing human-robot interaction beyond audio-only dialogue. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: A real-time system enabling social robots to proactively initiate dialogue based on user nonverbal cues.
card.key_idea: A multi-label recognizer using V-JEPA2 and a ViT-based architecture detects nine key nonverbal behaviors, which are then fed as tokens into an LLM for conditioned utterance generation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation (0.8 micro-F1) and offline intent agreement (49.1%) against teleoperator data from a 6-day real-world store deployment.
card.limitation: Struggles with rare task-related directives and lacks end-to-end online evaluation with user-experience metrics across diverse store environments.

slides.title: Real-time Generation of Listener Nodding via Prediction of Kinematic Parameters for Avatar Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This research proposes a model for predicting the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding in real time, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A real-time model predicting both the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding for conversational avatars.
card.key_idea: Dyadic attention networks using Continuous Mimi Encoders predict nodding onset and kinematic parameters (range, speed, repetitions, swing-up), with the parameter module fine-tuned from the timing module.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via five-fold cross-validation on an attentive listening dataset and subjective user ratings (n=60), significantly outperforming stochastic and fixed-motion baselines.
card.limitation: Subjective evaluations were conducted by third-party observers of videos rather than through direct, face-to-face interactions with the avatar.

slides.title: ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge: Multimodal Detection of Errors and Anticipation in Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: This work introduces datasets for detecting bystander reactions and anticipatory facial responses to robot failures, contributing to the development of robust error detection systems for RwB.

card.one_liner: The ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge introduces datasets for multimodal error detection and anticipation in human-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Two raw video datasets (BAD and Bad Idea) enable end-to-end ML models to detect bystander reactions and anticipate failure outcomes.
card.evaluation: Three teams submitted models that outperformed CNN baselines using crowdsourced, naturalistic video data.

slides.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition
slides.highlight: CF-Net utilizes cross-modal incongruence and speaker normalization to detect ambivalence and hesitancy, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: CF-Net recognizes ambivalence and hesitancy by explicitly modeling cross-modal incongruence using frozen multimodal backbones.
card.key_idea: Uses ConflictFusion (pairwise absolute-difference features), per-speaker normalization to remove identity offsets, and certainty-weighted focal loss with an auxiliary regression head to handle annotation ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BAH dataset; achieved 0.7155 validation Macro F1 and 0.7364 private test Macro F1, outperforming several 10th ABAW challenge methods.

slides.title: CausalGraphX: A Counterfactual Graph Neural Network Framework for Explainable Systemic Risk Assessment
slides.tldr: EXPLAINABLE SYSTEMIC RISK ASSESSMENT VIA COUNTERFACTUAL GNNs
slides.highlight: This framework uses counterfactual reasoning and Graph Neural Networks to model cascading defaults in financial networks, supporting the MIMIC goal of societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: CausalGraphX uses counterfactual GNNs to predict and provide actionable explanations for systemic financial risk cascades.
card.key_idea: Combines Graph Attention Networks with adversarial regularization to learn causal representations and an optimization-based generator to produce sparse, plausible counterfactual interventions for bank defaults.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic ER and BA networks against LR, DebtRank, GCN, and GAT; showed superior AUC, F1-score, and counterfactual plausibility.
card.limitation: Evaluated primarily on synthetic datasets rather than real-world financial data due to data scarcity.

slides.title: Learning Speaker Identity Beyond Language and Modality Constraints: Insights from the POLY-SIM 2026 Challenge
slides.highlight: This work addresses speaker identification challenges involving missing audio-visual modalities and multilingual speakers, supporting HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: The POLY-SIM 2026 challenge benchmarks multimodal speaker identification under missing-modality and cross-lingual constraints.
card.key_idea: A competition using MAV-Celeb (English-Urdu) to evaluate models on four protocols: in-language multimodal, missing-modality, cross-lingual multimodal, and cross-lingual missing-modality.
card.evaluation: 18 teams were evaluated on P-accuracy. Top team MaskedFOP achieved 99.89% average accuracy, significantly outperforming the FOP baseline (73.37%).
card.limitation: Top models relied on unsupervised adaptation using test-time input data, which is unrealistic for unheard target languages.

slides.title: Bloome Vs Traditional Multi-Agent Workflows: An AI Agents Group Chat Evaluation
slides.highlight: This evaluation of AI agent group chats and multi-agent workflows informs MIMIC's development of societal-scale simulations using LLM-based agent models.

slides.title: Same Stories, Different Journeys: From Social Comparison to Sensemaking in AI-Mediated Peer Career Exploration
slides.highlight: This work introduces JobMate, which transforms social media posts into conversational AI agents to shift passive browsing toward active engagement and constructive self-reframing. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and the modeling of human-AI interaction states.

card.one_liner: JobMate transforms social media career posts into persona-grounded AI agents to reduce harmful upward social comparison.
card.key_idea: A system that converts real user-generated content into conversational agents using a multi-stage pipeline, persona cards foregrounding challenges, and dual-track RAG for emotional and informational support.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing JobMate to native RedNote browsing. Results showed significantly lower cognitive effort (p=0.012) for similar reductions in career decision-making difficulties.
card.limitation: The study used a small sample size (N=24) and a short session, potentially limiting the generalizability of long-term effects.

slides.title: Human-Robot Interaction in GenAI Architectures via the Agent-Client Protocol
slides.tldr: UNIFIED COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL FOR GENAI-DRIVEN HRI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a decoupled three-layer architecture using the Agent-Client Protocol to standardize human-robot interaction, supporting real-time observability and task interruption. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A decoupled three-layer robotic architecture using ACP and MCP to standardize human-robot interaction and execution.
card.key_idea: Combines the Agent-Client Protocol (ACP) for the HRI layer and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for the execution layer, separating user interfaces, cognitive orchestration, and physical control.
card.evaluation: Tested on 'Sancho' mobile robot with three heterogeneous interfaces; validated real-time HRI workflows with negligible protocol latency (<0.5% of total loop time).
card.limitation: Lacks native support for continuous multimodal data streaming (e.g., live video) and asynchronous background telemetry monitoring.
